contract: Road user a is parked: "the standing of a vehicle, whether occupied or not", observed as a at rest at every observation of the window behind the observation, of length min_duration: at each of them a's speed (kin.speed, read through drv.motion.complete_halt) is at or below speed_tol. A halt shorter than min_duration, which may be the temporary halt the definition leaves out, is not denoted. It denotes a state at one observation: it says nothing of whether a rider is on a, of where a stands, or of why it stands. Not denoted: a road user whose speed was above speed_tol at some observation of that window. Where the window reaches before the start of the recording or a speed in it is unobserved, it is unknown.

params.name: speed_tol
params.meaning: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution

params.name: min_duration
params.meaning: the length of the window behind over which the road user must have been at rest: the longest halt that still counts as a temporary one

elements.span: a at rest at every observation of the window behind the observation, of length min_duration
elements.justification: drv.motion.complete_halt: 'The road user is at rest at the observation ... observed as its speed (kin.speed) at or below a tolerance the caller sets'; holding it at every observation of a window behind (holdsFor over time) is the standing the definition names, 'whether occupied or not', so no occupancy is read.

residues.span: otherwise than temporarily for the purpose of and while actually engaged in loading or unloading of merchandise or passengers
residues.why: a purpose is not observable; the definition's exclusion of a temporary halt is read only by the halt's duration (min_duration): a halt held longer than min_duration while loading is denoted, a halt shorter than it for any purpose is not

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle stands at rest beside the curb at every observation of the window behind, with no rider on it.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle halts briefly and moves off again within the window behind: its speed is above the tolerance at some observation of the window.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The source supplies no speed for the bicycle during the window.

contract: Road user a travels clockwise about the reference point of region r, as seen from above: the point lies to the right of a's direction of travel and a's velocity turns about it clockwise. It is observed with a's position (kin.position), a's velocity (kin.velocity), a's speed (kin.speed) and r's reference point (st.region_geometry), in the world frame, in which a turn to the left is counter-clockwise (the frame of kin.yaw_rate): with d the vector from r's reference point to a's position, the cross product of d with a's velocity is negative, and its square exceeds sin_tol squared times the squared length of d times the square of a's speed, so that the share of a's motion that turns about the point is above sin_tol; and a's speed is above speed_tol. It is a state at one observation: it says nothing of whether a occupies r, of the path a followed before, or of why a moves so. Not denoted: a road user at rest or moving at or below speed_tol; one travelling counter-clockwise about the point; one moving towards or away from the point within the angle sin_tol allows; one at the point itself. Where r's reference point, a's position or a's velocity is unobserved, it is unknown.

params.name: speed_tol
params.meaning: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement

params.name: sin_tol
params.meaning: the share of the speed, across the line to the reference point, at or below which motion counts as towards or away from the point rather than around it

elements.justification: kin.position: 'position of the body's reference point', world frame; the vector from r's reference point to it is d.
kin.velocity: 'velocity vector', world frame; its cross product with d gives the sense of travel about the point.
kin.speed: 'magnitude of velocity'; it bounds the share of the motion turning about the point and excludes a road user at rest.

st.region_geometry: 'the reference point and the boundary polygon of a structure region in the world frame'; the reference point is the point travel is judged about. Not a stand-in for occupancy: the concept reads no footprint.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: A car moves around the reference point of the region keeping the point on its right, its velocity mostly across the line to the point.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: A car moves around the reference point keeping the point on its left (counter-clockwise).

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The region is mapped without its reference point and boundary.

segmentation.text: It shall be unlawful for any person to operate
is reasonable and prudent under the conditions then existing

elements.justification: kin.speed: 'magnitude of velocity'. To operate a bicycle is read through its controlled motion (ontology, what is not an atom: 'operates' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion): the rule applies while the bicycle moves, its speed above the halt tolerance.

'bicycle' is admitted as the aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle ('a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride ... except a moped'); ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate'. Claimed as the aggregate, never expanded into classes.
kin.speed: 'magnitude of velocity', m/s; the speed the words compare with the reasonable and prudent bound. Not a stand-in for acceleration: none is read.

operationalizations.standard: a speed reasonable and prudent under the conditions then existing
operationalizations.convention: bicycle stopping-sight-distance model: the distance travelled during the perception-reaction time plus the braking distance at a deceleration set by the surface does not exceed the distance ahead the rider can see; the surface (dry, wet or precipitation, ice or snow) selects the deceleration, and darkness caps the distance seen at the reach of a bicycle headlamp

applicability: The subject belongs to the aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle and moves: its speed (kin.speed) is above p.halt_speed_tolerance.
obligation: At each such observation the subject's stopping distance does not exceed the distance it can see ahead. Stopping distance: speed times p.bicycle_reaction_time plus speed squared over twice the deceleration, where the deceleration is p.bicycle_decel_ice where env.ice_or_snow holds, else p.bicycle_decel_wet where env.wet_road or env.precipitation holds, else p.bicycle_decel_dry (a selection among bounds, Term.cond). Distance seen: env.visibility, and where env.darkness holds the smaller of env.visibility and p.bicycle_lamp_reach. Written as a product bound (speed squared at most twice the deceleration times the distance seen minus the reaction distance), so no measured atom is a divisor. Surrogate: its verdict is evidence, not a legal conclusion.

narrowings.why: 'any person to operate' is read through the bicycle's controlled motion: a bicycle moving on the road is taken to be operated, whoever rides it.

The catch-all 'the conditions then existing' is read only through the contracts the operationalization names: visibility, the wet, precipitation and ice states of the surface, and darkness. Other conditions (the sight distance a bend or a crest leaves, the presence and density of pedestrians and other traffic, grade, the bicycle's own condition) are not read, so a speed made unreasonable only by them is not detected.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle rides fast in dense fog: env.visibility is far shorter than the reaction distance plus the dry braking distance at its speed.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle rides at a moderate speed on a dry road in daylight with long visibility and sight distance, its stopping distance well inside both.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The bicycle stands at rest at a signal: its speed is at the halt tolerance.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The bicycle rides at a speed whose verdict depends on the visibility, which the source does not observe.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: On an icy road in light mist the bicycle rides at a speed whose stopping distance at the ice deceleration exceeds the visibility, though the dry stopping distance would not.

param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition standard's kinematic channel

param_proposals.name: p.bicycle_reaction_time
param_proposals.convention: perception-reaction time of a bicyclist in the stopping-sight-distance model
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Guide for the Development of Bicycle Facilities (2012), stopping sight distance

param_proposals.source: AASHTO Guide for the Development of Bicycle Facilities (2012), stopping sight distance

param_proposals.name: p.bicycle_decel_wet

param_proposals.source: AASHTO Guide for the Development of Bicycle Facilities (2012), stopping sight distance

segmentation.text: The operator of a bicycle, electric bicycle, or electric scooter
within a business or residence district
entering into or emerging from an alley, driveway or building
shall stop such vehicle immediately prior to
driving onto a sidewalk or onto the sidewalk area extending across any alleyway, driveway or building
yielding the right-of-way to any pedestrian
as may be necessary to avoid collision

elements.justification: Each term is admitted as its aggregate: 'bicycle' DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle ('a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride'), 'electric bicycle' DEF-LVMC-11-02-082::electric_bicycle ('a device upon which a person may ride ... an electric motor'), 'electric scooter' DEF-LVMC-11-02-083::electric_scooter ('a device with handlebars and an electric motor'); the subject belongs to one of them (same words as the mapping index's 'Any person operating a bicycle, electric bicycle, or electric scooter'). 'The operator' is read through the device's controlled motion.

rel.occupies: 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'; st.alley: 'a narrow way within a block serving the rear of properties'; st.driveway_or_alley_entrance: 'private road, alley or driveway meeting the highway' (its 'not a stand-in' clause, which of them meets the highway, does not matter: alley and driveway are both named); st.highway: 'the entire public way between its boundary lines' — a road user that occupies no highway region is beyond the property line, where a building stands. Read at the entry onto the sidewalk: emerging = at the observation before the entry the subject occupies an alley or a driveway/alley entrance, or occupies no highway region; entering into = at the entry the subject occupies an alley or a driveway/alley entrance (the sidewalk area extending across it), or from the entry it occupies the sidewalk until it occupies no highway region (the movement into a building read by the movement itself).

Same words as the mapping index (LVMC_11_20_060_o1): drv.motion.complete_halt, whose definition DEF-NRS-484A-255 applies to 'Stop, when required' ('complete cessation from movement'); the stop is required here, so DEF-NRS-484A-260 (stopping when prohibited) does not apply. 'such vehicle' refers back to the device the subject operates; it is not a new class condition (the vehicle definition DEF-NRS-484A-320 excludes devices moved by human power, electric bicycles and electric scooters, so reading it as a class would empty the duty). 'immediately prior to' places the halt in the stopping zone just short of the sidewalk, read with e5.

Same atoms as the mapping index's 'driving onto a sidewalk or onto the sidewalk area extending across any alleyway or driveway'. st.sidewalk: 'area for pedestrians between roadway and property line' (not a crosswalk: none is meant); rel.occupies marks the event, the footprint coming to overlap the sidewalk; st.region_geometry: 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it' bounds the stopping zone outside the sidewalk. The sidewalk area across an alleyway, driveway or building is a part of a sidewalk region.

applicability: The subject is a bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter (any of the three aggregates). For a sidewalk region s, at the observation at which the subject's footprint comes to overlap s (rel.occupies(subject, s) there and not at the observation before), asm.business_or_residence_district holds and the subject enters into or emerges from an alley, driveway or building: at that observation or the one before it occupies an st.alley or st.driveway_or_alley_entrance region; or at the observation before it occupies no st.highway region; or from that observation on it occupies s until it occupies no st.highway region.
obligation: Act before an event (rule 4c). Event: the entry onto sidewalk s defined in the applicability. Place: the stopping zone of s, the observations at which the subject does not occupy s and the ground distance from its body to s (st.region_geometry) is at most p.stop_point_tolerance. Act: drv.motion.complete_halt(subject; p.halt_speed_tolerance) at an observation in that zone. Search: from the observation before the event back through the observations at which the subject's body stays within p.stop_point_tolerance of s; it ends at the last observation before the event at which the subject is farther than p.stop_point_tolerance from s (the approach start) or at the last observation at which it occupied s (its previous entry onto s, whose halt does not count for this one). A halt found in the zone within the search: compliant. The search reaching either end without a halt: violated. Where it reaches neither end without a halt, because the recording begins inside the zone or the distance to s or the occupancy of s is unobserved at an observation the search crosses: unknown. A reverse, a lateral move or a speed fluctuation inside the zone begins no new approach. The halt is read on s itself, the sidewalk the event enters; no other sidewalk stands for it.

narrowings.why: 'The operator' is read through the device's controlled motion: whoever or whatever controls it, the device's conduct is judged.

'immediately prior to' is read as a halt in the stopping zone of the sidewalk being entered, outside it and within p.stop_point_tolerance of it, during the approach that leads to the entry (the ontology's convention for an act due at a place before an event); a halt made farther back does not discharge the duty.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: In a declared residence district a bicycle rides out of a driveway entrance and onto the sidewalk without its speed falling to the halt tolerance while within the stopping zone; it was farther than the tolerance from the sidewalk earlier in the recording.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same bicycle halts just short of the sidewalk, within the stopping zone and outside the sidewalk, then rides onto it.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: An electric scooter rides along the sidewalk from one sidewalk region into the next, coming from the sidewalk, not from an alley, a driveway or off the public way.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle emerges from a driveway onto the sidewalk with no halt recorded, and the source maps regions without their outline, so the stopping zone and the approach start cannot be read.

scenarios.name: history_boundary
scenarios.narrative: The recording begins with the electric bicycle already within the stopping zone, moving out of a driveway; it enters the sidewalk with no halt recorded, and the search reaches the start of the recording without reaching the approach start.
scenarios.boundary: the subject's approach to the sidewalk: the last observation at which it was farther than p.stop_point_tolerance from the sidewalk lies before the recording

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The same driveway exit without a halt, in a place the map's reading declares outside any business or residence district.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition standard's kinematic channel

param_proposals.name: p.stop_point_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the body-to-mark gap within which a halt counts as at the mark: a stop line's set-back before a crossing plus a placement margin
param_proposals.source: MUTCD stop-line placement practice

segmentation.text: The operator of a bicycle, electric bicycle, or electric scooter
within a business or residence district
entering into or emerging from an alley, driveway or building
shall stop such vehicle immediately prior to
driving onto a sidewalk or onto the sidewalk area extending across any alleyway, driveway or building
yielding the right-of-way to any pedestrian
as may be necessary to avoid collision

elements.justification: Each term is admitted as its aggregate: 'bicycle' DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle ('a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride'), 'electric bicycle' DEF-LVMC-11-02-082::electric_bicycle ('a device upon which a person may ride ... an electric motor'), 'electric scooter' DEF-LVMC-11-02-083::electric_scooter ('a device with handlebars and an electric motor'); the subject belongs to one of them.

As in LVMC_11_40_140_o1: rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'; st.alley 'a narrow way within a block serving the rear of properties'; st.driveway_or_alley_entrance 'private road, alley or driveway meeting the highway'; st.highway 'the entire public way between its boundary lines' (occupying none of it: beyond the property line, where a building stands). Read at the subject's latest entry onto the sidewalk it occupies.

Same atoms as the mapping index for these words. st.sidewalk 'area for pedestrians between roadway and property line'; rel.occupies: the subject's footprint on that sidewalk since its entry; st.region_geometry is claimed with the words as mapped and reads the sidewalk's outline for the occupancy the source derives.

'yielding' as in the mapping index: kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' (the subject proceeds only while it does not create a conflict) and rel.contact 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)'; not a stand-in for a near miss, which the standard e7 bounds. 'pedestrian' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'). The right-of-way (DEF-NRS-484A-210) is 'the right ... to proceed ... in preference to another' approaching so as 'to give rise to the danger of a crash'.

operationalizations.standard: as may be necessary to avoid collision
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: while the subject moves, a pedestrian whose centre comes, under constant velocities, within the conflict clearance of the subject's centre within the conflict horizon is a danger of collision the subject must yield to

applicability: The subject is a bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter. At an observation at which it occupies a sidewalk region s and has occupied s at every observation since its latest entry onto s (rel.occupies(subject, s) since the observation at which it rose), where at that entry asm.business_or_residence_district held and the subject entered into or emerged from an alley, driveway or building (as in LVMC_11_40_140_o1: at the entry or the observation before it occupied an st.alley or st.driveway_or_alley_entrance region; or at the observation before it occupied no st.highway region; or from the entry it occupies s until it occupies no st.highway region).
obligation: For every pedestrian p of the scene other than the subject (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian): the subject is not in contact with p (rel.contact), and it is not the case that the subject's speed is above p.halt_speed_tolerance while prim.closest_approach_within(subject, p; p.conflict_horizon) holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, p; p.conflict_horizon) below p.conflict_centre_clearance. A scene with no pedestrian is compliant.

narrowings.why: 'The operator' is read through the device's controlled motion.
Yielding is read as not proceeding into a conflict and not colliding: the subject may move where no pedestrian is in conflict with it; where one is, it must be at rest.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: In a declared business district a bicycle emerges from a driveway onto the sidewalk and keeps moving while a pedestrian walking along the sidewalk is on a course whose closest approach falls within the conflict horizon and the clearance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same bicycle halts on the sidewalk area and waits while the pedestrian passes, then moves on once the closest approach no longer falls within the clearance.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The bicycle rides on the roadway past the driveway and never occupies the sidewalk.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle near a driveway with a pedestrian approaching, where the source does not observe which regions the bicycle occupies.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: An electric scooter emerges from an alley across the sidewalk with no pedestrian in the scene: the duty binds the subject alone and is met.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition standard's kinematic channel

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: Hydén, The development of a method for traffic safety evaluation: the Swedish Traffic Conflicts Technique (1987)

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
param_proposals.source: passenger-car design dimensions (AASHTO Green Book design vehicle)

segmentation.text: It shall be unlawful for any person to park
a bicycle, electric bicycle, or electric scooter
other than upon the roadway against the curb
in a rack to support the bicycle, electric bicycle, or electric scooter
in such a manner as to afford the least obstruction to

elements.justification: 'park' is defined by DEF-NRS-484A-155 ('the standing of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, otherwise than temporarily for the purpose of and while actually engaged in loading or unloading'); drv.motion.parked carries that definition: at rest at every observation of a window behind of length min_duration. The definition's word 'vehicle' is the thing parked, here the device the words name; its purpose clause is read by the halt's duration.

Each term is admitted as its aggregate (DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle 'a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride'; DEF-LVMC-11-02-082::electric_bicycle; DEF-LVMC-11-02-083::electric_scooter); the parked device belongs to one of them.

'street' (DEF-NRS-484A-265) is 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every highway inside the territorial limits of a city'; st.highway: 'the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders' (not a stand-in for the roadway: the whole width is meant, as the definition says). rel.occupies anchors the device on it. The city-limits clause is the ordinance's own territorial scope: the City's code applies only within the City, so the condition is the same inside the reading's domain.

st.roadway: 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder' (DEF-NRS-484A-220); rel.occupies anchors the device on it; st.road_edge: 'curb or edge of the roadway'; rel.contact: 'the bodies of ... a road user and a structure, touch or overlap' — 'against the curb' is the device's body touching the curb.
st.sidewalk: 'area for pedestrians between roadway and property line' (DEF-NRS-484A-240); rel.occupies anchors the device on it. Not a crosswalk.

Nearest atoms only (gap): st.obstruction kind sidewalk_fixture is 'a physical object on or beside the roadway that is not a road user' of any fixture kind; it does not tell a rack built to hold a bicycle from a pole, a bench or a sign post, so reading it as the rack would permit parking against any fixture.

Nearest atoms only (gap): no structure atom carries a building; st.highway's boundary is the property line, not a wall, and st.obstruction is an object on or beside the roadway, not a building, so 'against a building' has no region for rel.contact or st.region_geometry to read.

st.road_edge: 'curb or edge of the roadway'; st.region_geometry: 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it' — 'at the curb' on the sidewalk is the device's body within p.parked_edge_reach of the curb. Distance here is what the words require (at the curb), not a stand-in for belonging.

'pedestrian traffic' is the pedestrians among the traffic (DEF-NRS-484A-285 'pedestrians, ... vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway'): the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair ...') carries them; the other members of traffic are not the ones whose obstruction the words name.

operationalizations.standard: in such a manner as to afford the least obstruction to pedestrian traffic
operationalizations.convention: curbside placement practice: a parked bicycle obstructs pedestrian traffic least when its body lies within a placement margin of the curb or wall it is parked at, out of the walking path, and no pedestrian walking by comes into contact with it

applicability: The subject is a bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter that is parked (drv.motion.parked(subject; p.halt_speed_tolerance, p.parking_min_duration)) while it occupies an st.highway region (a street).
obligation: At each such observation the subject stands at a permitted place: (a) it occupies an st.roadway region and is in contact (rel.contact) with an st.road_edge region (against the curb); or (b) it occupies an st.sidewalk region and is in a bicycle rack [gap], or in contact with a building [gap], or within p.parked_edge_reach (st.region_geometry distance) of an st.road_edge region (at the curb). And it stands so as to afford the least obstruction to pedestrian traffic: no pedestrian (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) is in contact with it, and on the sidewalk its body lies within p.parked_edge_reach of the curb or of the building it is parked at.

narrowings.why: 'any person to park' is read through the device's standing; the definition's 'otherwise than temporarily for the purpose of and while actually engaged in loading or unloading' is read by the halt's duration (p.parking_min_duration), since the purpose of a halt is not observed.

'least obstruction' is comparative; it is read as the device standing within the placement margin of its edge with no pedestrian in contact with it, not as the least obstruction any placement could achieve, and the width of walkway left free is not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle stands at rest, longer than the parking duration, in the middle of the roadway, touching no curb.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle stands at rest longer than the parking duration on the roadway with its body touching the curb, and no pedestrian touches it.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle is ridden along the street and never stands at rest for the parking duration.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The bicycle stands at rest on the roadway beside the curb, and the source does not observe contact between road users and structures.

param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition standard's kinematic channel

gaps.proposal: `st.bicycle_rack` | a fixed stand on a sidewalk or beside the roadway built to hold parked bicycles and the devices a jurisdiction groups with them, with its outline, so that a device held in it is read by rel.contact or rel.occupies **Not a stand-in for:** any other sidewalk fixture (a pole, a bench, a sign post) | general
gaps.nearest: st.obstruction kind sidewalk_fixture — any fixture: it does not tell a rack from a pole or a bench, so it cannot decide where the law permits parking on the sidewalk

gaps.proposal: `st.building` | a building beside the highway, carried as a region with its outline (the face of its wall toward the way), so that contact and ground distance from a road user to it are read through rel.contact and st.region_geometry **Not a stand-in for:** the property line or the boundary of the highway | general
gaps.nearest: st.highway — its boundary is the property line, not a wall; st.obstruction — an object on or beside the roadway, not a building; neither decides whether a device is parked against a building

segmentation.text: It shall be unlawful for any person to ride
a bicycle, electric bicycle, or electric scooter
on Fremont Street between Main Street and Seventh Street
This area shall be posted with signs indicating that the riding of bicycles, electric bicycles, or electric scooters on the sidewalk is prohibited

elements.justification: Riding is read through the device's controlled motion: a device ridden moves, so the duty is that the device be at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt: 'The road user is at rest at the observation ... its speed (kin.speed) at or below a tolerance'), as the mapping index reads 'shall be ridden' (LVMC_11_38_030).

Each term is admitted as its aggregate (DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle 'a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride'; DEF-LVMC-11-02-082::electric_bicycle 'a device upon which a person may ride ... an electric motor'; DEF-LVMC-11-02-083::electric_scooter 'a device with handlebars and an electric motor'); the subject belongs to one of them.

st.sidewalk: 'area for pedestrians between roadway and property line' (DEF-NRS-484A-240); rel.occupies: 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region' anchors the subject on it. Same atoms as the mapping index's 'upon any sidewalk'.

assumptions.meaning: the place of the road user at the observation lies on Fremont Street between Main Street and Seventh Street, as the map's reading records the named way and its limits

residues.why: The sentence directs the City to post signs; the riding prohibition of the first sentence holds whether or not the signs are posted, so the duty is the same either way.

applicability: The subject is a bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter that occupies an st.sidewalk region (rel.occupies) at a place where asm.fremont_street_main_to_seventh holds.
obligation: At each such observation the subject is at rest: drv.motion.complete_halt(subject; p.halt_speed_tolerance).

narrowings.why: 'any person to ride' is read through the device's controlled motion: a device moving on the sidewalk is read as ridden, so a device pushed by a person walking beside it is not told apart from one ridden (no rider posture is read).

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: An electric scooter moves along a sidewalk at a place the map's reading declares to be Fremont Street between Main Street and Seventh Street.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle stands at rest on that sidewalk.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle rides on the roadway of Fremont Street within the declared stretch, never on the sidewalk.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle on that sidewalk whose speed the source does not supply.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle rides on a sidewalk at a place the map's reading declares outside the named stretch.

segmentation.text: The Director of Public Works is authorized to erect signs
bicycles, electric bicycles, or electric scooters

when the Director after consultation with the City Traffic Engineer and the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department determines that the use of bicycles, electric bicycles, or electric scooters on the sidewalk or roadway in question will impede or interfere with the flow of pedestrian or vehicular traffic
and when such signs are in place
it shall be unlawful for any person to disobey the same

elements.justification: dev.regulatory_sign: 'a point regulation by catalogue code'; the authority to erect the sign is its legal status, read by the sign's presence on the road (status reading).

Nearest atoms only (gap): st.sidewalk 'area for pedestrians between roadway and property line' and rel.occupies anchor the subject, but dev.governs relates a device only to 'travel regions ... never a highway, a controlled-access region or a region no vehicle travels in', and a sidewalk is none of the kinds it lists, so no atom ties a sign to the sidewalk it is erected on.

st.roadway: 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic' (DEF-NRS-484A-220); rel.occupies anchors the subject on it; dev.governs: 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls — ... roadway' ties the sign to that roadway (not a position: the sign's place is not read).

dev.regulatory_sign with code bicycles_prohibited: the catalogue's sign prohibiting bicycles, read as the sign the words describe, which prohibits riding by all three classes (status reading). Not a stand-in for a manoeuvre: the sign is the condition.
Each term is admitted as its aggregate (DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle; DEF-LVMC-11-02-082::electric_bicycle; DEF-LVMC-11-02-083::electric_scooter); the subject belongs to one of them.
'thereon' ties the sign's prohibition to the sidewalk or roadway it is erected on: dev.governs between the sign and the roadway the subject occupies (rel.occupies).

The Director's determination is the legal basis of the sign; the sign's presence on the road is the evidence of it (ontology, legal status of a feature: 'a rule reads the feature and presumes the status'). The determination's content (pedestrian or vehicular traffic flow) names no road user the duty turns on.
'in place': the sign is present and governs the region (dev.governs 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'); where governance is unobserved the rule is unknown.

Disobeying a riding prohibition is riding where it governs: the subject moves (not drv.motion.complete_halt, 'at rest ... speed at or below a tolerance') while it occupies (rel.occupies) the governed region.

residues.why: 'by any person' sets no restriction: every rider of the three classes is bound, which the subject span already states.

applicability: The subject is a bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter that occupies a region g where asm.within_city_limits holds, g being an st.roadway region (or a sidewalk region [gap]) governed (dev.governs) by a dev.regulatory_sign of code bicycles_prohibited.
obligation: At each such observation the subject is at rest on g: drv.motion.complete_halt(subject; p.halt_speed_tolerance). The same g, bound with the same sign and governance, is the one the subject occupies.

narrowings.why: The Director's authority to erect the sign is read by the sign's presence.
The Director's determination after consultation is read by the presence of the sign it authorizes.
'any person to disobey' is read through the device's controlled motion: a device moving on the governed region is read as ridden there; one pushed by a walking person is not told apart.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Within the declared city limits a bicycle rides along a roadway governed by a bicycles_prohibited regulatory sign.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: An electric bicycle stands at rest on that governed roadway.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle rides on a roadway no bicycles_prohibited sign governs.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle rides on a roadway near a bicycles_prohibited sign, and the source does not observe which regions the sign governs.

gaps.proposal: `dev.governs_walkway` | relation: the sidewalk regions whose use a sign erected for them controls — a sign prohibiting riding on a sidewalk governs that sidewalk and nothing else; unknown where the source does not observe it **Not a stand-in for:** a position, or the travel regions dev.governs relates | general
gaps.nearest: dev.governs — 'never a highway, a controlled-access region or a region no vehicle travels in': it does not relate a sign to a sidewalk, so where the riding prohibition applies on a sidewalk is undecided; dev.position / st.region_geometry — distance never stands for belonging

segmentation.text: Whenever any person is riding a bicycle, electric bicycle, or electric scooter upon a sidewalk

elements.justification: The three terms are admitted aggregates (DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle; DEF-LVMC-11-02-082::electric_bicycle; DEF-LVMC-11-02-083::electric_scooter). 'riding' is read through controlled motion: the device is not at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt false). 'upon a sidewalk': st.sidewalk 'area for pedestrians between roadway and property line', anchored by rel.occupies.

'shall yield' as in the mapping index: kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' (the subject does not proceed into a conflict) and rel.contact 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)'.
'pedestrian' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair ...'); same mapping as the index's 'to any pedestrian'.

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: preference over another approaching 'under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash' (DEF-NRS-484A-210)
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: a pedestrian whose centre comes, under constant velocities, within the conflict clearance of the moving subject's centre within the conflict horizon is approaching so as to give rise to the danger of a crash

applicability: The subject is a bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter that occupies an st.sidewalk region (rel.occupies) and is not at rest (not drv.motion.complete_halt(subject; p.halt_speed_tolerance)).
obligation: For every pedestrian p of the scene other than the subject (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian): the subject is not in contact with p (rel.contact), and it is not the case that prim.closest_approach_within(subject, p; p.conflict_horizon) holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, p; p.conflict_horizon) below p.conflict_centre_clearance. A scene with no pedestrian is compliant.

narrowings.why: 'any person is riding' is read through the device's controlled motion: a device moving on the sidewalk is read as ridden.
Yielding is read as not proceeding into a conflict and not colliding: while riding, the subject keeps every pedestrian outside the conflict bound.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle rides along the sidewalk toward a pedestrian walking toward it; their closest approach falls within the conflict horizon and below the clearance, and the bicycle keeps riding.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle rides along the sidewalk; a pedestrian on it walks away on a diverging course whose closest approach stays above the clearance.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle rides on the roadway beside the sidewalk where pedestrians walk.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle moves near a pedestrian, and the source does not observe which regions the bicycle occupies.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: An electric scooter rides on an empty sidewalk with no pedestrian in the scene: the duty binds the subject alone and is met.

segmentation.text: Whenever any person is riding a bicycle, electric bicycle, or electric scooter upon a sidewalk

elements.justification: As in LVMC_11_40_180_C_o1: the three admitted aggregates; 'riding' read through controlled motion (not drv.motion.complete_halt); st.sidewalk 'area for pedestrians between roadway and property line', anchored by rel.occupies.

sig.horn: 'an ordinary horn ... sounding (audible)'; sig.siren: 'a siren, whistle or bell sounding (audible)' — a bicycle bell or a whistle is the latter, a horn the former; either sounding is an audible signal. Neither is read from a visible state ('no visible state stands in for it'); a source without audio declares them absent, and the rule is then unknown.

drv.interaction.overtake_pass: 'Road user a overtakes and passes road user b from the rear: a, travelling in the same direction as b, comes from having b ahead of it to having b behind it'. 'before' is read with the same relations the concept states: the pedestrian ahead of the subject (rel.bearing longitudinal component positive, rel.longitudinal_overlap negative) with headings aligned (rel.same_direction), during the run of observations that ends at the act's onset.
'such pedestrian' refers back to 'any pedestrian': the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot ...'), the road user b of the pass.

applicability: The subject is a bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter. For a pedestrian p of the scene (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian, not the subject), at the observation at which drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, p; p.overtake_window, p.overtake_same_direction_cos) holds (the pass is recognized), where at some observation while the pass was under way (from its onset to its recognition) the subject occupied an st.sidewalk region and was not at rest.
obligation: Act before an event (rule 4c). Event: the onset of the pass, the last observation of the window behind at which p was ahead of the subject with headings aligned (rel.bearing longitudinal component positive, rel.longitudinal_overlap negative, rel.same_direction with p.overtake_same_direction_cos), read with atLast over p.overtake_window. Act: sig.horn or sig.siren sounding for the subject. Search: from the onset back through the run of observations at which p stays ahead of the subject; it ends at the observation at which that run began (p came to be ahead), which is the approach start, or at the recognition of a previous pass of p by the subject. A signal found in the search: compliant. The search reaching its start without a signal: violated. Where the run began before the recording, or the signal or the relations are unobserved at an observation the search crosses, without a signal found: unknown. A signal given while p is alongside or after it is behind does not discharge the duty.

narrowings.why: 'any person is riding' is read through the device's controlled motion.
An audible signal is read as a horn, bell or whistle sounding (sig.horn, sig.siren); a spoken warning has no atom, so a rider who warns only by voice is read as giving no signal.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle rides on the sidewalk behind a pedestrian walking the same way, draws alongside and passes, and no horn, bell or whistle sounds while the pedestrian is ahead of it; the pedestrian came to be ahead within the recording.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same pass, with the bicycle's bell sounding while the pedestrian is still ahead of it.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle rides on the sidewalk behind a pedestrian at the same pace and never passes.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The same pass with no signal in the trace, from a source without audio that declares horn and bell absent.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: An electric scooter begins the pass on the roadway edge and moves onto the sidewalk while alongside the pedestrian, completing the pass there without any signal.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: An electric scooter rides on the sidewalk, leaves it for the roadway before drawing alongside, and passes a pedestrian on the sidewalk from the roadway without signal: it is on the sidewalk only before the act began.

scenarios.name: history_boundary
scenarios.narrative: The recording begins with the pedestrian already ahead of the bicycle on the sidewalk; the bicycle passes without a signal in the recording, and the search reaches the start of the recording without reaching the observation at which the pedestrian came to be ahead.
scenarios.boundary: the run of observations with the pedestrian ahead of the rider begins before the recording

segmentation.text: shall be in a counterclockwise direction

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', excluding human-powered devices, electric bicycles, electric personal assistive mobility devices and electric scooters, which the aggregate's reading classifies). 'operation' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

st.roundabout: 'a rotary intersection: its central island, its circulatory roadway and its entry and exit approaches' — the roundabout of DEF-LVMC-11-02-130 ('the area bounded by the outermost curb line ... and includes the crosswalks on any entering or exiting roadway'); rel.occupies anchors the subject in it.
'vehicular' is the vehicle aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'travel' is motion: the vehicle not at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt false).

drv.motion.circulating_clockwise_about: 'Road user a travels clockwise about the reference point of region r, as seen from above'; counterclockwise travel is its negation, with the motion towards or away from the point within the tolerance left undecided by neither sense. The circulatory roadway is the part of the roundabout 'used by vehicles to travel counterclockwise around a central island' (DEF-LVMC-11-02-040): the sense is judged about the roundabout's reference point.

applicability: The subject belongs to DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, occupies an st.roundabout region r (rel.occupies) and is not at rest (not drv.motion.complete_halt(subject; p.halt_speed_tolerance)).
obligation: At each such observation, for the roundabout r the subject occupies: not drv.motion.circulating_clockwise_about(subject, r; p.halt_speed_tolerance, p.roundabout_clockwise_sin_tol). The same r bound in the applicability is the one the concept reads.

narrowings.why: Counterclockwise is judged about the reference point of the roundabout region, read as the centre of its central island; motion towards or away from that point within the tolerance (entering, leaving) is not clockwise and so is compliant.
'the operation of vehicles' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car in a roundabout circulates keeping the central island on its right, clockwise about the roundabout's reference point.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A car circulates keeping the central island on its left, counterclockwise.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car drives on a straight street with no roundabout.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car circulates in a roundabout that the source maps without its reference point and outline.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: An electric scooter circulates clockwise in the roundabout: electric scooters are excluded from the vehicle definition.

param_proposals.convention: the share of a vehicle's speed across the line to the roundabout's centre at or below which its motion counts as towards or away from the centre rather than around it: within about 15 degrees of the radial direction
param_proposals.source: roundabout entry and exit path geometry (FHWA Roundabouts: An Informational Guide, NCHRP Report 672)

segmentation.text: to vehicles already in the roundabout

elements.justification: 'vehicles' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'operation' read through controlled motion.

st.roundabout 'a rotary intersection: its central island, its circulatory roadway and its entry and exit approaches' (DEF-LVMC-11-02-130's area, crosswalks of the entering and exiting roadways included); rel.occupies anchors the subject: at its entry it occupies the roundabout.
'a vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'The operator' read through the vehicle's controlled motion.
Entering is the event at which the subject's footprint comes to overlap the roundabout (rel.occupies true and false at the observation before); st.roundabout is the region entered.
'shall yield' as in the mapping index: kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' and rel.contact 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)'.

'vehicles' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'already in the roundabout': each occupies (rel.occupies) the roundabout region r the subject enters at the observation before the entry and at the entry.

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: preference over another approaching 'under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash' (DEF-NRS-484A-210)
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: a circulating vehicle whose centre comes, under constant velocities, within the conflict clearance of the entering vehicle's centre within the conflict horizon is approaching so as to give rise to the danger of a crash

applicability: The subject belongs to DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, and at the judged observation it enters an st.roundabout region r: rel.occupies(subject, r) holds there and not at the observation before.
obligation: At that entry, for every road user v of the scene other than the subject that belongs to DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle and occupies r at the observation before the entry and at the entry: the subject is not in contact with v (rel.contact), and it is not the case that prim.closest_approach_within(subject, v; p.conflict_horizon) holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, v; p.conflict_horizon) below p.conflict_centre_clearance. An entry with no such vehicle is compliant.

narrowings.why: 'The operator' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.
Yielding is judged at the entry: the subject enters only where no vehicle already in the roundabout is in conflict with it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car enters the roundabout while a circulating car, already in it, is on a course whose closest approach to the entering car falls within the conflict horizon and below the clearance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A car enters the roundabout while the only circulating car is on the far side, its closest approach above the clearance.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car circulates inside the roundabout throughout the recording without entering it.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car near the roundabout's edge beside a circulating car, where the source does not observe which regions the cars occupy.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A car enters an empty roundabout: no other vehicle is in the scene, and the duty is met.

segmentation.text: to vehicles already in the roundabout

elements.justification: 'vehicles' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'operation' read through controlled motion.
st.roundabout 'a rotary intersection: its central island, its circulatory roadway and its entry and exit approaches'; rel.occupies anchors the subject: at its entry it occupies the roundabout.
'a vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'The operator' read through the vehicle's controlled motion.
Entering is the event at which the subject's footprint comes to overlap the roundabout region (rel.occupies true and false at the observation before).

'wait ... before entering' is a condition on the entry: the subject's footprint comes to overlap the roundabout (rel.occupies of st.roundabout) only where the gap holds; waiting where none holds is staying out of it.

'traffic' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances either singly or together using any highway for purposes of travel'); the traffic of the gap is the traffic in the roundabout the subject enters (rel.occupies of that st.roundabout region, crosswalks of its entering and exiting roadways included).
'before entering' fixes the moment: the observation at which the subject's footprint comes to overlap the roundabout region, the same event as b5.

operationalizations.standard: a gap in traffic sufficient to enter
operationalizations.convention: gap-acceptance convention of roundabout entry capacity: an entering driver accepts a gap when no road user in the roundabout comes, under constant velocities, within the conflict clearance of it sooner than the critical headway

applicability: The subject belongs to DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, and at the judged observation it enters an st.roundabout region r: rel.occupies(subject, r) holds there and not at the observation before.
obligation: At that entry, for every road user u of the scene other than the subject that belongs to DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic and occupies r: the subject is not in contact with u (rel.contact), and it is not the case that prim.closest_approach_within(subject, u; p.roundabout_critical_gap) holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, u; p.roundabout_critical_gap) below p.conflict_centre_clearance. An entry with no such road user is compliant.

narrowings.why: 'The operator' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.
'wait for a gap' is read as entering only at a gap: where a gap is present when the subject arrives no halt is required, and an entry without a gap is the failure to wait.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car enters the roundabout while a pedestrian on one of its crosswalks is on a course whose closest approach to the car comes within the clearance sooner than the critical gap.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A car waits at the edge and enters once no road user in the roundabout comes within the clearance of it within the critical gap.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car drives on a street away from any roundabout.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car at the roundabout's edge beside circulating traffic, where the source does not observe which regions the road users occupy.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A car enters an empty roundabout: no other road user is in the scene, and the duty is met.

param_proposals.source: Highway Capacity Manual, 6th edition, roundabouts chapter
